description: Labeled incidents for the deep-investigation (autonomous orchestrator) eval. Keyed by service name, shared across the live bigdata-cluster stacks. The DANGEROUS failure modes are what the labels gate: a cross-infra-type category error (wrongCausePatterns) or a fabrication. A grounded, on-type cause is CORRECT even if it isn't the one signal we first guessed — these services can be healthy on one axis (e.g. Consul) while failing on another (their own daemon / a real dependency). acceptableInconclusive lists honest non-confirmed outcomes (a healthy service SHOULD decline, not invent a cause).

labels.summary: Bare-metal Consul-registered service. Correct = its Consul health failing, OR a grounded impala-internal cause (daemon/query/catalog/statestore). WRONG = a k8s framing (it has no Deployment by design).

Bare-metal Consul-registered service. Correct = Consul health failing OR a grounded internal/dependency cause (DB, disk, a real upstream). WRONG = a k8s framing. Distinct from the k8s service 'bd-management-task'.
Bare-metal Consul-registered service (Apache Kudu master). Correct = Consul health failing OR a grounded kudu-internal cause (tablet/disk/memory). WRONG = a k8s framing.
Bare-metal Consul-registered service (HDFS NameNode). Correct = Consul health failing OR a grounded namenode-internal cause (disk/block/journal/rpc). WRONG = a k8s framing.
Kubernetes workload (kube_deployment identity metric). A correct cause is a deployment/pod/replica/container-level fault; a Consul-health cause is a category error here.
Kubernetes workload (kube_deployment). Distinct from the Consul service 'bd-management-task-management' — a category-error test: its correct cause is k8s-shaped, and a Consul cause is wrong.
